Middleware before the handler: just that one global `express.json()` body parser. Nothing captures or preserves the raw body.

Rejected requests: HTTP 400, JSON body `{"error": "No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload"}`. The `PayCo-Signature` header on rejected requests is present and well-formed (`t=<ts>,v1=<hex>`) — it's just never matching.

Likely root cause on our end: when verify() is handed a non-string/non-Buffer payload, the SDK falls back to `JSON.stringify(payload)` to recompute the HMAC. Re-serializing an already-parsed object won't byte-for-byte match whatever raw bytes you originally signed (key order, number formatting, whitespace can all differ), so the HMAC never matches no matter how correctly you signed it. We reproduced this locally with our own test harness — even signing and verifying against our own secret fails the same way once the payload passes through `express.json()` first — which points at our body handling, not your signing.
